set.brief: Owner's design idea for ux/Dictate, 2026-10-01 (part of the same 'Clean mode' thread, see /framework/ai/2026-10-01/clean-dictate-mode/ — related but a separate, smaller piece): a new mic-state indicator to replace the current level-meter bar (`level: true`, which needs a fixed height). Owner's words, assembled from several passes: 'when you're on the page... maybe there's a kind of a darkened [state]... some visual cue that it's not listening. And then when you tap kind of like anywhere in the chat feed, it kind of unlocks it, but also turns it on... a little orange dot, the primary color, pretty small, but then kind of just grows, bounces... instead of using the levels indicator we have now... a little sphere that bounces/grows, it stays in place but fluctuates, the size of it pulses with the audio. So when the microphone is on you see the orange dot and as you speak it grows. Maybe you can tap on it. It should be pretty small so it's unobtrusive, bottom right corner maybe.' So: default state = darkened/locked (mic off), tapping anywhere in the chat feed unlocks AND turns the mic on; while live, a small dot in the site's primary color sits bottom-right, pulsing/growing in size with the live audio level (replacing the level-meter bar's job, no fixed-height bar needed), and is itself tappable (presumably to stop). Scope this as a new Widget option alongside the existing `level` meter (keep the existing one reachable, CLAUDE.md 'never destroy a viable version'), read ux/Dictate/readme.md and Widget.js/Widget.css and Dictate.js's on_meter level-reading first, propose the concrete mechanics briefly, implement, verify with a screenshot (talk into the mic, see it pulse), and land per finish-task.
